videos.title: Freight moves. The observer stays.
videos.caption: Customer freight moves. An observer stays aboard. Volvo and Waabi announced Warp customer operations along the Dallas to Houston corridor, carrying freight directly to third-party facilities. The companies plan additional routes. The release reports customer service with an occupied cab. It does not supply independently audited safety or efficiency results.

videos.title: The clue had to move
videos.caption: An AI candidate still needed a living test. Texas Children's and Baylor researchers used fly experiments to test a BRSK1 clue after standard genetic analysis came up empty. A normal human gene largely restored movement. Patient variants restored only part of it. The comparison supports a likely diagnosis, not a treatment.

videos.title: The warmer unit
videos.caption:
FacilityOps AI says its Houston inspection pilot found a failed condenser. A handheld check confirmed the measurement. The vendor reports that the condenser was repaired and the unit returned to normal operation.

A second cooling unit showed intermittent temperature spikes. That condition was flagged for inspection, not confirmed as a fault.

The vendor's September 23rd update describes an ongoing pilot. This film uses generic illustrations. A robot's flag starts a maintenance check. It doesn't finish one.

videos.title: Before the robot moves
videos.caption: UT Austin researchers propose a robot safety filter learned from expert demonstrations. The filter would change a proposed action before the robot moves. Spoken feedback could slow the robot near fragile glass. Physical experiments and user studies are planned. This film is an original illustration of the research plan rather than proven protection.

videos.title: Before the next watering
videos.caption:
Texas Tech's July 6th announcement describes planned crop-water trials with AgriLife. Drone, ground and satellite observations would enter one database. Machine learning would predict crop growth under different irrigation conditions. Irrigation recommendations and water savings are goals. This film illustrates the planned research.

#TexasAI #Agriculture #Water

videos.title: The second point of contact
videos.caption: A packed trailer can hide a carton's top. Austin startup Contoro describes a gripper that holds two surfaces at once, with AI planning and remote human backup. Original illustrations show the company-described workflow and its limits.

videos.title: Before the valve opens
videos.caption: Rice plans a Houston laboratory where AI could rehearse experiments in a digital twin before using physical equipment. NSF backed READINESS in July. The project would learn from results and consult a researcher when uncertain. Diamond thin films are among its targets. Rice describes a planned laboratory.

videos.title: Below the dark mark
videos.caption: Texas State researchers pair pavement images with depth maps to separate damage from stains. A prioritized repair report does not repair the road.

videos.title: Before the package lands
videos.caption: A package descending is only half the delivery. Zipline's proposed pod workflow can retract when a landing spot is unsuitable. The FAA draft covers Austin and four other Texas cities. The expansion still needs approval. Comments are open through October eleventh.

videos.title: The camera count is not the fire count
videos.caption: In a report covering part of 2025, Southwestern Public Service lists 33 AI wildfire cameras installed in the Texas Panhandle. The regulator asked for a fire-detection count. The report gives an equipment count instead. A missing count does not mean zero detections. #TexasAI #TexasPanhandle #Wildfire

videos.title: The recording is still a test
videos.caption: Womb Watch is recruiting in Austin, Houston and Galveston to study phone recordings and AI estimates of fetal movement. Noise can mean recording again. Researchers are assessing daily use and participants' anxiety. The app's results remain experimental and non-diagnostic. #TexasAI #HealthResearch #Austin

videos.title: The lease behind the well
videos.caption:
Can an oilfield engineer pull up the lease behind a well? Battalion Oil says its planned Collide deployment would connect well files and contracts in one searchable model. The company sees a fit at Monument Draw in Ward County, but integration, staff adoption and better drilling decisions remain unproved.

The film illustrates the proposed records workflow. It does not show an operating Battalion system.

videos.title: A notice changes a day
videos.caption: Dallas brush-truck cameras capture curbside images for review. The city says a person participates in every action. NBC reports courtesy notices went to thousands of owners. Sarrah Morrison told NBC a notice sent her outside to clean in extreme heat. Her case outcome was unreported.

videos.title: The vote that did not come
videos.caption: Denton held its first hearing on a proposed data-center moratorium, but council took no vote. CBS News Texas reported that all twenty speakers supported the proposed pause. The local proposal would halt acceptance, processing and approval of new applications if adopted. Separately, Governor Greg Abbott directed TCEQ to halt data-center permits pending an ERCOT audit. Denton has scheduled a second hearing for October 27th. The film uses illustrative animation, not footage of the hearing.

videos.title: The empty seat is an invitation
videos.caption: Aurora offered attendees a ride on one segment of its active Dallas to Houston driverless freight route. The filing shows an invitation, not a completed passenger trip. Aurora's reported miles show scale, while the cited sources leave a safety comparison with human drivers unanswered.

videos.title: Where the flies land
videos.caption: USDA describes AI models guiding screwworm surveillance and sterile insect releases. Animal transport remains a forecasting limit.

videos.title: What the eye misses
videos.caption: Two powders can look alike while absorbing light differently. Si-Ware announced its new Austin headquarters on September 17th. Its planned application lab aims to help robotics teams explore material sensing. The company's contact demonstration describes distinguishing sugar from flour and teaching an unfamiliar sample. The signal adds information. A real application still needs testing.

videos.title: Within reach
videos.caption: UT Austin's robot research aims to put useful assistance within reach. The announcement reports no care results.

videos.title: After the fax arrives
videos.caption: A medical fax still has to find the right patient chart. UTHealth Houston says its AI system handles parts of that filing work, extracting details and linking documents to records. Its September 16th report describes staff time saved, but gives no appointment waiting times. Does less filing lead to earlier care? That remains the next question.

videos.title: The rock goes in
videos.caption: SMU plans mineral testing in Navasota with AI and digital-twin training. Selected for award negotiations. No completed testbed or test results reported.

videos.title: Before the trouble travels
videos.caption: A Texas A&M research project in College Station starts today with a plan to build digital twins for freshwater systems. Sensor readings, weather and maintenance records would help models anticipate failures that spread. The NSF award describes planned tools and workshops for operators. It reports no measured service improvements. The real test still belongs at the pump.

videos.title: The case still has work
videos.caption: On September 8th, Kodiak reported 93 percent highway safety case readiness through August. That measures claims and evidence it considers materially complete, not the probability of a safe trip. Its June filing names Texas as the initial driverless launch market. Existing Dallas to Houston freight service is a separate fact. Year-end remains a company target, with the highway safety case unfinished.

videos.title: Before it turns the fan
videos.caption: On September 1st, the University of Houston announced federal support for AI-guided permanent-magnet research. The plan pairs compound predictions with synthesis predictions, then physical testing. More reliable domestic sourcing is the goal. Commercialization remains a milestone.

videos.title: The proof decides
videos.caption: Rice University's new NSF-backed project will let AI propose numerical algorithms, then use Lean to check their correctness and cost claims. The award starts September 15. The real story is the gate between a machine proposal and reusable mathematics.

videos.title: The warning stays local
videos.caption: UT San Antonio researchers built a field-ready flood-warning prototype that keeps evaluating sensor data when power, cell service and cloud links fail. The inference happens on the node, then LoRa carries a report to a local hub. Initial validation is not a deployed warning network, and field weatherization still comes next.

videos.title: The seat stays empty
videos.caption: An empty seat is the point of today's Dallas-Fort Worth air taxi tests. Joby's electric aircraft flies with a pilot while a separate aircraft demonstrates autonomy. Texas says this phase carries no passengers. The flights are for route validation and operational evidence before later rider stages can move under FAA oversight. Watch the flight log before the promise.

videos.title: The clock that has not started
videos.caption: Houston Methodist compared discharge-date estimates from case managers and an artificial intelligence model. At admission, case managers named the exact date more often, while the model's absolute error was similar. The study did not test whether either estimate improved patient outcomes, and the model was available in the health record but not automatically shown to clinicians.

videos.title: The clock that has not started
videos.caption: Brownsville commissioners voted to begin drafting a possible data-center moratorium. The moratorium is not in effect. The proposed path includes a public hearing, impact reports and a final vote, with any approved pause taking effect only after that process.

videos.title: Before the match
videos.caption: At Progreso, a live pedestrian facial-biometric assessment tested whether cameras could capture usable images before any match. DHS says capture exceeded expectations, but its public account gives no accuracy rate, retention period, or final deployment choice.

videos.title: What the ground still holds
videos.caption: A free field day near Ralls puts irrigation equipment and questions in the same field on September 9th. Autonomous Pivot is on the program. The illustrated system turns reflected signals, crop images and weather into irrigation advice. The announcement reports no measured water-saving result. That leaves a practical question for the farmer standing beside it.

videos.title: The loop begins with a question
videos.caption: An unfinished alloy sample enters a planned loop in Bryan. Robots will melt, shape, heat-treat and test it while researchers keep the hypothesis, interpretation and metallurgical judgment. The agreement starts now. The first user call has not.

videos.title: The grade the machine had to clear
videos.caption: A reaper drawn on the gate around a drilling floor in Midland, and the grade the machine had to clear.

videos.title: The only machine you can check
videos.caption: Horizon, the public supercomputer, has its first half running in a redeveloped call centre off a frontage road in Round Rock, and the operator's own user guide says access is limited to internal users. What makes a public machine public was never its size.
